abstract: This paper examines political advertising and coordinated behavior on social media during the run-up to the 2021 German federal elections. It investigates how political actors used advertisements and potentially coordinated activity across social media platforms in this electoral context. The study contributes to understanding the interplay between paid political messaging and coordinated online behavior in a major European election.
key_claims: Political advertising and coordinated behavior were notable features of the social media environment preceding the 2021 German federal elections.
Analyzing paid advertisement alongside coordinated activity offers insight into how political communication operates on social media during elections.
methods: Empirical analysis of social media data related to the 2021 German federal elections (specific methods not available from the abstract alone).
findings: Specific findings are not available from the abstract provided.
contributions: Provides an examination of political advertisement and coordinated behavior in the context of the 2021 German federal elections.
Adds to the literature on coordinated inauthentic or coordinated online behavior in European electoral settings.
framing: The paper is situated within research on political communication, social media influence, and coordinated behavior in the context of democratic elections.
